5. BUS RAPID TRANSIT (BRT)
Source: https://www.cairo.gov.eg/en/governorate-services/transportation-services/bus-rapid-transit/
Page last updated: June 2026. The portal describes electric buses on dedicated Ring Road lanes, approximately 10-minute intervals, station access by pedestrian tunnels or bridges, and displays showing arrival information. It describes a 106 km route with possible extension, 49 stations, 36 in phase 1, approximately 100 electric buses and estimated cost 9.5 billion EGP. It also mentions 24-hour operation in three shifts, park-and-ride, minibus access roads and connections to metro, trains and SuperJet; these are source descriptions/plans, not independently verified current service hours.
Source station table, in its displayed row order (not necessarily route order):
Marshal Tantawi; Cairo Festival City; Police Academy; Suez Road; Adly Mansour; 10th of Ramadan Stop; Gharb El-Rashah; El-Trolley; Zakat Foundation; Masraf Belbeis; Metwally El-Shaarawy; Ahmed Orabi; Ezbet El-Gazira; Al-Assar; Ard El Lewa; El-Marg; Mantai; 26th of July Axis; Rashah El-Khusus; Alexandria Agricultural Road; Al-Motamadiya; Mostorod; Bassous; Zenin; El-Bahr El-Aazam; Bassous Al-Qanater; Saft El-Laban; El-Zahraa; Al-Warraq; Manshiyat El-Bakari; El-Ezba; Tahya Misr; Al-Noor; Mehwar Al-Hadarah; Imbaba Metro; Al-Madina Mosque; El-Gazaer; Bashtil; Faisal; Al-Autostrad; Al-Talbiya; Al-Haram; El-Hadaba El-Wosta; Al-Mounib; Tersa; City Centre Maadi; Al-Talbiya; EgyptAir; Shooting Club; Al-Baron; El-Shaheed Axis; Tagamoa Entrance.
Al-Talbiya appears twice in the source table. The number of displayed entries and its stated 49-station project count do not match; the table should not be treated as a verified route sequence.
Fares stated: 4 stations 5 EGP; 9 stations 10 EGP; 14 stations 15 EGP. The first phase is described as Alexandria Agricultural Station to Police Academy Station. The source describes 76 km of first-phase Ring Road expansion, including Mariouteya/Mounib to Alexandria Agricultural Road and Mansouria/Fayoum intersection to Wahat Road; later BRT phases depend on further expansion. Four charging stations are planned, including one at Adly Mansour; the design includes main charging centers at the ends of the line.

4. LIGHT ELECTRIC TRAIN (LRT)
Source: https://www.cairo.gov.eg/en/governorate-services/transportation-services/light-electric-train/
Page last updated: 2026. The project links the New Administrative Capital with the Cairo/Giza area. The source lists:
Phases 1 and 2: Adly Mansour; Obour; Mostakbal; El Shorouk; New Heliopolis; Badr. From Badr the page describes a north branch to Industrial Zone and 10th of Ramadan (1), and a south branch to El Robbiki; Capital Gardens (Badr El Gedida / New Badr); Administrative Capital (1) — Capital Airport; Administrative Capital (2) — City of Arts and Culture.
Phases 3 and 4 listed in the station table: Administrative Capital (3) — Cathedral of the Nativity of Christ; (4) — Strategic Command Center / The Octagon; (5) — Sports City; (6) — Central Station; 10th of Ramadan (2), (3), (4).

Tickets sold at counters or vending machines: 3 stations 10 EGP; 7 stations 15 EGP; more than 7 stations 20 EGP. Monthly subscriptions: 3 stations 300 EGP; 5 stations 500 EGP; 7 stations 600 EGP.
The page says phases 1–2 opened on 3 July 2022, covered 68.81 km and 12 stations, and ran from Adly Mansour to City of Arts and Culture. Adly Mansour connects LRT, Metro Line 3, railway, SuperJet and BRT. Branded minibuses connect nearby communities; parking and Capital buses linking City of Arts and Culture to the Government District are described. The page claims a 15-minute interval and free station parking; check current availability.
Phase 3, described as under construction: 20.4 km from Cathedral of the Nativity to Central Capital, 4 stations (3 elevated and 1 surface): Cathedral of the Nativity, Strategic Command Center, International Sports City, Central Capital. A high-speed rail interchange is planned at Central Capital.
Phase 4, described as under construction: 16 km north from New Obour to City Center, with West 10th of Ramadan, 10th of Ramadan and City Center stations. The source quotes 7.2 km elevated and 9.3 km surface, which do not add exactly to 16 km. The station naming differs between its table and phase description.
Phase 5: proposed 7.8 km extension, one station, from New Administrative Capital station across Cairo–Ain Sokhna Road to the capital's industrial zone; the page reports an MoU with AVIC.
The page describes overhead electricity supply, energy storage, parking and environmental/operating benefits; its comparisons are project claims, not independently verified here.

LINE 4 — construction/planning as described by the source, not confirmed live status: 42 km and 39 planned stations (37 underground, 2 surface), expected capacity about 2 million passengers per day. The route starts west of the Ring Road near 6th of October City, runs past the Grand Egyptian Museum and Remaya Square along Al Haram Street to Giza (planned interchange with Line 2), then to El Malek El Saleh (Line 1), Magra El Oyoun, Salah Salem Street, El Nasr Road, Al Mokawloon Al Arab Club, Nasr City and El Rehab, ending at an integrated transport center north of the Ring Road/Cairo–Suez Road junction.
Phase 1: 19 km, 17 stations, Hadayek El Ashgar to Fustat; via the museum, Remaya Square, Al Haram and Giza; crosses the Nile to El Malek El Saleh. Phase 2: 23 km, 22 stations, Fustat to Nasr City and New Cairo, via Salah Salem, Mansheyet Nasser, El Doweiqa, El Arab District, Al Mokawloon Al Arab Club, Railway Club, Al-Azhar University, El Shaheed Axis, Mostafa El Nahhas Street, El Teba, Mahdi Arafa Street, El Methaq Street, Zahraa Nasr City, the Police Academy and Mostafa Kamel Axis near El Rehab, ending near Cairo–Suez Desert Road and the workshop. text:
Application: visit a subscription office, complete the relevant form with two 4 × 6 cm photos, supply ID or birth certificate and any applicable membership documentation, and obtain the relevant authority's stamp; general public applications do not require a stamp. Student forms need Student Affairs approval, the prescribed photo stamps, ID/birth certificate, proof of tuition payment or current/previous academic-year card, and a phone number when required. Student passes cover the residence-to-study route. Passes are personal and misuse can incur a penalty.
Student form: https://www.cairometro.gov.eg/ (follow the form link from the source page).
Quarterly offices — Line 1: Helwan, Ain Helwan, Helwan University, Maadi, Dar El Salam, El Zahraa, El Shohadaa, Hadayeq El Zaitoun, Ain Shams, Ezbet El Nakhl, Old Marg, New Marg. Line 2: Faculty of Agriculture, El Mazallat, Rod El Farag, Massara, El Shohadaa, Ataba, Dokki, Cairo University, Giza, El Mounib. Line 3: Ataba, Abbassia, Heliopolis, Adly Mansour.
Annual offices — Line 1: Helwan, Maadi, Ain Shams. Line 2: Faculty of Agriculture, Rod El Farag, El Shohadaa, Ataba, Cairo University. Line 3: Heliopolis, Adly Mansour.
Cash wallet: anonymous, reusable smart card for single trips; initial card price 80 EGP; recharge denominations listed from 40 through 500 EGP. The page says it can be shared, has no fixed use period and is sold at all stations on the three lines.

6. MONORAIL
Source: https://www.cairo.gov.eg/en/governorate-services/transportation-services/monorail/
The portal describes electric trains on elevated single-rail beams, two East and West Nile lines, and an 80 km/h operating speed. It presents project benefits including lower congestion, pollution and fuel consumption and support for new urban development. Current operations and construction progress should be checked with the operator.

The page labels the following 16 stations inaugurated, with its numbering:
1 Field Marshal Tantawy; 2 Al-Mostasmerin; 3 Al-Lotus; 4 One Ninety; 5 Beit Al-Watan; 6 Al-Fattah Al-Aleem Mosque; 7 Air Force Hospital; 8 R2 Residential District; 9 R1 Residential District; 10 Justice City; 11 Government District; 12 Misr Mosque; 13 Financial District; 14 Golden Square; 15 Al-Narges; 16 Arts and Culture City.
The source separately describes the East Nile line from Field Marshal Tantawi to Justice City, serving Nasr City, New Cairo and the New Administrative Capital. It mentions an LRT interchange at Arts and Culture City and future interchanges with Metro Line 6 at El Narges and phase 2 of Line 4 at Hesham Barakat. The separately numbered station table should not be assumed to be a route sequence, since the source's endpoint and table ordering are not fully consistent.

West Nile line: the page describes 43.8 km from 6th of October City to Wadi El Nile in Mohandessin, serving the city's southern developments. Its 13 named stations are New October; Ahram Canadian University; Sadat; 6th of October University; Engineers Syndicate; Mall of Egypt; Sheikh Zayed City; Alexandria Road; Mansouria; Mariouteya; Ring Road; Bashteel; Wadi El Nile. It names Alstom and Arab Contractors among the consortium. Listed interchanges: Metro Line 3 at Wadi El Nile; Upper Egypt Railway Station at Bashteel; Ain Sokhna–Marsa Matrouh high-speed rail at Engineers Syndicate Club; and a future Line 4 phase at 6th of October University.
